claims.statement: The hosted workflow processes project evidence locally in the browser and exposes no hosted generation endpoint.
Device-local storage retains at most 25 projects and ten packet versions per project, with a session-memory fallback.
Every generated ledger claim retains a supplied source and uncertain mappings remain marked Review.
Every valid V1 packet contains an implementation summary, stakeholder walkthrough, verification runbook, and Codex workflow skill.
Approved packets can be signed with a non-extractable device ECDSA P-256 key and independently verified from the embedded public key and signer fingerprint.
A matching SHA-256 checksum is classified separately from a valid asymmetric signature and is never presented as signer verification.
The optional Codex companion pins gpt-5.6-sol, denies approvals, disables network and web search, filters its environment through an allowlist, and starts in an isolated temporary working directory.
Production responses apply CSP, frame denial, MIME-sniffing prevention, a restrictive referrer policy, a permissions policy, and HSTS over HTTPS.
This release-claims artifact is attested only after installation, dry-forge validation, lint, tests, build, secret scanning, and claim-contract validation pass in GitHub Actions.

limitations: A valid ECDSA signature proves that the packet bytes have not changed since the holder of the corresponding private key signed them.
A signer fingerprint establishes identity only when the recipient compares it through an independent trusted channel.
Cryptography does not prove that supplied evidence is semantically true; source review and reproducible tests remain required.
GitHub artifact attestation proves repository, workflow, commit, and artifact provenance; the public workflow and test implementation remain inspectable inputs to that trust decision.
